titleStmt.title: The Secretary for Foreign Affairs to the American Ambassador.

head.hi: The Secretary for Foreign Affairs to the American Ambassador.

div.p: The undersigned has the honor to inform his excellency, Mr. David Jayne Hill, ambassador of the United States of America, in reply to the note of the 9th instant, that the Imperial Government is ready to lay before the Bundesrath a motion that the advantages of paragraph 46 of the potash law be extended to the contracts concluded by American purchasers previous to December 17, 1909. It may, however, be pointed out that the advantages to be granted must be kept within definite limits, since the legal provision in question is intended merely to offer foreign purchasers security that they will not be compelled, in consequence of the legal charges, to incur higher expenditures in the purchase of the salts than would be the case in buying salts not burdened with duties from another source.

Therefore, in calculating the average expenditures, including the reduced duties, which the purchaser has to pay out for the salts, the quantities not in excess of the quota of the seller and not burdened with the duty, must also be included.

list.item: Secondly. As was already stated in the note of the foreign office of May 11, the reduction can only be applied to quantities which the buyer can prove that he is obliged to accept, and not to quantities with respect to which he may exercise the right of option.

Thirdly. The buyer would have to petition for reduction of the duty to be paid by the seller, and at the same time furnish proof that he is not only bound to accept the goods, but to defray the duty also.

Lastly. The Imperial Government would not like to omit the suggestion that perhaps the proper moment has arrived for an amicable agreement between the American buyers, the potash works supplying them, and the other potash works, which would settle the question of levying a duty on the ground, of paragraphs 26 and 46 of the law. The Imperial Government would be ready to promote such an agreement as far as possible.
